objective: Record one product decision for the first household MVP baseline: name the three separate system stages, bound the MVP to one mobile base, one arm and one RGB-D sensor, state the required targets with source, owner and status, and explain the historical 55 kg and 6.42 kg numbers instead of blending them into one robot mass.
decision_supported: Can the household MVP be defined as one indoor mobile base, one arm/gripper, one RGB-D camera, one onboard compute and one safety MCU without inheriting the dual-arm U-cell, the tabletop fixture, or an unmeasured UR5e mobile claim?
acceptance: The P0 fixed-tabletop simulator, the fixed development bench and the household product are named as three separate stages with their own identifiers and owners.
The household MVP is bounded to the scenarios in #159, #163 and #164 plus navigation #152, and to one mobile base, one arm/gripper, one RGB-D camera, one onboard compute and one safety MCU.
The one-arm baseline is explicit and dual-arm coordination is out of MVP scope.

Payload, reach, doorway width, base footprint, tip/stability margin, total mass, battery/runtime, compute, sensor and safe-speed targets each state a value or an explicit gap, a source path, an owner and a status.
The UR5e is labelled bench hardware; the record states that no measured mobile payload or stability evidence approves it for the product and that no implicit arm swap is claimed.

The historical 55 kg dual-arm U-cell ledger and the 6.42 kg compact enclosure model are explained as separate superseded systems and are not blended into a single robot mass; the 77.5 kg Revision D analytical model stays the only current total.
Resource-budget hooks point to #79 and require ROS 2, Nav2, MoveIt and perception measurements with the local Ollama route disabled by default.
Guarded appliance open/close is phase 2 (#160); elevators, stairs, public lockers, outdoor travel, bimanual coordination and arbitrary deformable or fragile objects are later phases.
Superseded scope statements link to this record, and accepted ADR-0001 and ADR-0004 are not rewritten.

The Product, Motion, Integration, Safety and Hardware owner approvals are recorded as an explicit fail-closed register that keeps the record proposed until each owner approves or raises a blocking objection.
A static regression test fails if the stage separation, the required target rows, the historical-mass explanation, the bench-hardware label, or the fail-closed approval rule is removed.
evidence: Task Packet validation output for the single packet and for every committed packet against origin/main.
Static regression test output covering the stage separation, the ten required target rows, the historical-mass explanation, the bench-hardware label and the fail-closed approval register.
make context-check and strict make docs build output.
Full repository make test output and the final whitespace audit.
docs/decisions/ADR-0007-household-mvp-baseline.md itself, including the target table and the approval register.
stop_conditions: A product, mechanical, procurement, safety or release decision would need to be invented rather than recorded as proposed or requested.
A change would require editing CAD, design-spec.json, the mass ledgers, robot control, firmware, the PCB package, interfaces or public schemas.
Any target value would need to be invented because no committed source states it; record the gap instead.
A historical 55 kg or 6.42 kg number would be presented as the current household MVP mass.
An owner approval, a physical measurement or a target-hardware resource result would need to be fabricated.
data_classification: Public repository documentation only; no personal, partner, procurement or supplier-identifiable data.
model_policy: Neither a language model nor this document may approve scope, procurement, safety or release; the local Ollama route stays out of the MVP resource baseline unless a named owner decides otherwise.
risks_and_fallbacks: This record defines a baseline and cannot create a physical robot; every target stays an estimate, a gap or a requested approval until measured evidence exists.
If an owner raises a blocking objection, keep the record proposed and the household MVP blocked rather than resolving the objection in documentation.
If a required target has no committed source, record the gap and its owner instead of extrapolating a number.
